summary.intent: Build a verified evidence base and work-package plan for front-end/design-ideation support in the wisp-plugins repo, then decide how to expand plugins/skills/agents and review the architecture against current agent platform capabilities (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity).
summary.outcome: Committed a 144-work-package catalog locally, answered the structure question (add skills/agents in muse and smith, defer a new plugin), then added an ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md with 16 more work packages (160 total), ADR N11, and a corrected constitution premise. The branch push was denied, so nothing is published.

repo: Each of the 44 agents embeds one identical 6-line <constitution> block (one distinct hash). The 290-line shared/constitution.md is an authoring-time rulebook that only the mason auditor reads at runtime, so earlier claims of a 290-line copy per agent were wrong.
`just check` runs tests, version agreement and mermaid validation; the reference-integrity test flags proposed new reference files unless they are marked with a <refs>/ placeholder.

New skills and agents need a Codex counterpart and `just marketplace-sync` per shared/harness-authoring.md; agents also need the 5-part structure (ADR 001) and constitution (ADR 006); renaming a plugin or skill needs a new ADR (ADR 007).
Codex has its own native plugin format in harnesses/codex/, while AGY's plugin format is similar to Claude Code's and shares the authored tree.

Platform cache prefixes are shared only by requests with the same model, effort, agent type, tools, schema and working directory, so a byte-identical constitution saves little across differently configured agents (inference from research).
Claude Code plugin-shipped agents ignore hooks, mcpServers and permissionMode; agent descriptions share a 15,000-token total budget.
workflow: Relative paths after a cd into a subfolder led to a stray CATALOG.md at the repo root; use absolute paths and verify with pwd and git status after appends.
Subagent research reports mixed primary reads with search summaries and 403-blocked pages, so tags like [P]/[S]/[U] were needed to weigh claims.
Measure the repo directly before accepting research assumptions: counting the constitution block overturned a premise carried through earlier notes.
Remove the tool artifacts you created (e.g. .playwright-mcp) only after confirming they are untracked and match your own activity.

friction: git push was denied by the permission classifier as an out-of-place publication, so the branch remains local.
Several vendor pages (openai.com, Antigravity) returned 403, leaving many Codex, Cursor and Copilot claims resting on secondary sources.
The shell's working directory drifted into the evaluation folder, causing a mis-targeted append and a duplicate cat/append command to clean up.
Earlier figures in the plan (296 tests, 32 stalled, llms.txt prevalence, Coinbase numbers) were found unsupported and had to be corrected.
just check output scrolled off, requiring a separate just test run to confirm tests passed.

Confirm wave order (Wave 1 exploration before Wave 2 gate hygiene) and whether sketch/promote live in muse or a new plugin.

Run the constitution/backstory ablation (WP-62) and tier measurements (WP-63) before adding the three new agents.
Re-verify the AGY marketplace.json schema reference, and whether Codex loads .claude-plugin formats.
Re-check the generated Codex tree against Agent Plugins 1.0.0 extensions.com.openai namespacing.
Author AGY skills only, since workflows stop working 2026-10-19.
Unverified items remain: pages commit counts, Shopify/Airbnb figures, ICAO terminology, rtk workflow question, JetBrains Air, Primer, Windsurf and Warp.
Decide whether muse:critic is a separate agent or an auditor mode, and whether muse:copy becomes a skill.
